meta.name: Chase overdue invoices and match bank payments with Gmail, Sheets, and OpenAI

name: Chase overdue invoices by customer and match bank payments with Gmail, Sheets and AI

parameters.content:
## Chase overdue invoices by customer and match bank payments with Gmail, Sheets and AI

### How it works

1. At 7am the bank lines are matched to open invoices: by the number in the reference, by an exact amount, or by the one combination that adds up. If two add up, a person decides.
2. At 9am the chase run works per customer, not per invoice: one statement for everything they owe.
3. Four rules stop a chase before it leaves: the invoice is in dispute, they promised a date still to come, their money is already with us unmatched, or the balance is under the floor.
4. The ladder never skips a rung, and a promise they broke moves it up one.
5. An account over its limit, or in dispute, goes to its account manager instead.
6. Collections is the one step it will not take on its own: it asks the finance lead and waits.
7. Replies are read as they arrive. A promise holds the next chaser back, a dispute stops it, and an out-of-office changes nothing.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect Gmail, Google Sheets and OpenAI credentials.
- [ ] Create one sheet with four tabs: Customers, Invoices, Payments, Chase log.
- [ ] Put the sheet ID and your addresses in all three Set nodes: the triggers never run together.
- [ ] Check the thresholds in Set Collection Policy against your own terms.

### Customization

Every threshold is in a Set node; the ladder, the grace days and the suppression rules are one Code node.

## Start the weekday chase run

Nine in the morning, Monday to Friday. **Set Collection Policy** is the only node in this branch you edit: the sheet ID, two addresses, and every threshold the decision below reads.

## Load customers, invoices and history

Four tabs, read once. Each **Aggregate** folds a read into a single item, because a Sheets node runs once per item it is handed: without them the next read repeats for every row.

## Decide who to chase today

The node this template exists for. One decision per customer rather than per invoice, and most of them are decisions not to write at all. The loop then takes them one at a time.

## Send one statement per customer

One email covering everything they owe, in the words the ladder allows. Three overdue invoices are three lines of a table here, not three emails to the same person on the same morning.

parameters.message:
=Hello,

{{ $json.statement }}

If any of this is wrong - an invoice you never received, a payment you have already made, a line you disagree with - reply to this email and say so. The replies are read.

Quoting the invoice number in your payment reference means it is matched the next morning and nothing further is sent.
parameters.subject: ={{ $json.subject_line }}

parameters.content:
## Escalate to the account manager

Over the credit limit, in dispute, or no address on file. The customer hears nothing today: the next contact comes from the person who owns the relationship, with the account's history in front of them.

parameters.subject: =Needs you: {{ $json.customer_name }} ({{ $json.currency }} {{ $json.amount_due }} overdue)

parameters.content:
## Ask before handing to collections

The one step this workflow will not take on its own. Finance gets the account's whole history and three days to answer, and a refusal is written to the log as plainly as an agreement.

parameters.subject: =Hand {{ $json.customer_name }} to collections?

parameters.content:
## Write the chase log

Every branch ends in one row: who, when, at what level, and why. That row is what the next run reads to know whether the gap has passed and which rung it is standing on.

## Start the payment matching run

Seven in the morning, two hours before the chase run, so that money which arrived overnight is matched to an invoice before anybody is asked for it again.

## Read payments and open invoices

The bank lines your bank or your bookkeeper drops into the Payments tab, and everything still open in Invoices. Rows already marked allocated are passed over, so the run is safe to repeat.

## Match payments to invoices

By the reference, by an exact amount, or by the one combination of their invoices that adds up. Two combinations that both add up mean a person decides, not the order of the rows.

## Write the balances back

The invoice takes its new balance, the bank line takes what it paid for. Each is matched on its own key, so running the morning twice rewrites the same rows instead of doubling them.

## Report what needs a person

One email, holding only what could not be settled: payers nobody recognises, short payments, overpayments and ties. Everything the run did work out is already in the sheet and not repeated here.

parameters.subject: =Bank matching: {{ $json.rows.length }} payment(s) need you

parameters.content:
## Catch replies to the chasers

Every reply to a chaser, read within fifteen minutes. **Set Reply Rules** carries the sheet ID a third time, because this trigger never runs in the same execution as the other two.

filters.q: in:inbox -from:me newer_than:30d subject:(invoice OR overdue OR payment OR reminder)

parameters.content:
## Read the reply with AI

The model is asked what the customer wants - a date, a dispute, a claim that it is already paid, a copy of the invoice - and told to copy their words rather than judge whether they are right.

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You are reading a customer's reply to a chaser about an unpaid invoice.

Copy what they wrote. Do not infer, do not calculate, do not decide whether they are right: somebody else does that, and they need your reading of the words, not your opinion of them.

A date is copied in the writer's own format. If a field is not in the reply, return an empty string - a blank is handled downstream, an invented date stops a genuine reminder for a fortnight.

Choose 'other' whenever the reply does not clearly fit one of the named intents.

attributes.name: intent
attributes.description: Exactly one of: promise (they say when they will pay), dispute (they say something is wrong with the invoice or the goods), paid (they say it is already paid), copy (they ask for a copy, a statement or details), other.

attributes.name: promised_date
attributes.description: The date they say they will pay, copied exactly as written. Empty string if they give none.

attributes.name: invoice_numbers
attributes.description: Every invoice number the reply mentions, separated by commas, exactly as printed. Empty string if none.

attributes.name: payment_reference
attributes.description: The payment or transfer reference they quote as proof of payment. Empty string if none.

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The date they say they paid, copied as written. Empty string if none.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: In their own words, what they say is wrong. Empty string if they are not disputing anything.

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: One sentence saying what this person wants, in plain words.

parameters.content:
## Work out what it means

Whether a person wrote it at all is settled by the headers, not by the model. A date counts as a promise only if it parses, has not passed, and is near enough to be a date rather than a wish.

## Apply the reply to Sheets

A promised date holds the next chaser back until it has passed. A dispute stops the chasing on that invoice outright. Both are written on the invoice row itself, where the next run will read them.

## Hand the rest to a person

Claims of payment, requests for a copy, and disputes worth a human answer. An out-of-office ends at the No Operation node and changes nothing, which is the whole point of checking the headers.

parameters.subject: =Dispute: invoice {{ $('Read What the Reply Says').item.json.invoice_number }}
=Reply needs you: {{ $json.from }}

parameters.content:
## Report a failure of the workflow

A fourth entry point, firing only when a production run errors. A silent failure in collections looks exactly like a month in which everybody happened to pay on time.

parameters.subject: =Collections workflow failed: {{ $json.execution.id }}
